newsitem.title: USA: U.S. banks getting bigger profits from securities.
newsitem.headline: U.S. banks getting bigger profits from securities.

text.p: U.S. banks recorded a 37 percent profit increase in the first quarter of 1997 from retail investment services compared with the fourth quarter of 1996, the Bank Securities Association said Tuesday.
The association said the increase reflected productivity improvements and increases in revenue and profit margins.
The association said the typical full-time licensed investment specialist in a bank generated gross commission revenues of $22,709 per month, up 4 percent from the fourth quarter of 1996.
The association said the average monthly gross for brokers selling in banks was up 23 percent from the first quarter of 1996.
The Bank Securities Association is a non-profit trade association.
The association said 28 financial institutions participated in the study of first-quarter activity. A spokesman said dollar amount figures were not immediately available.
